summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate of Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands-on experience bringing up, validating, and debugging embedded hardware platforms across STM32 microcontrollers, FreeRTOS real-time systems, and NVIDIA Jetson compute platforms. Built and instrumented custom hardware and software subsystems using oscilloscopes and logic analyzers, ran quantified performance benchmarking, and root caused integration failures through structured lab-based debugging. Comfortable across C/C++, Python, and Linux-based engineering environments, collaborating across hardware, firmware, and software teams.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed wearable gesture-recognition glove firmware integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth microcontrollers to translate hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented an interrupt-driven tap-detection algorithm; resolved sensor jitter through structured root cause debugging of the hardware-software interface.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Owned mechanical design and hardware bring-up end-to-end for a 25-member national-competition robotics team.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory testing environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation in a Linux-based engineering environment.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 microcontroller firmware in bare-metal embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing, interrupt-driven ADC1 sample capture, and a low-level I2C1 driver for real-time display.

Programmed peripherals directly (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1), achieving 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified functional correctness through lab-based design verification testing in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling for real-time operation and control on an STM32 microcontroller.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization for closed-loop hardware-software validation.
Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to the STM32 over UART for cross-subsystem coordination.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Replaced TorchScript convolution layers with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing and constant memory, then ran performance analysis benchmarking 49.2 ms coalesced versus 77.5 ms CPU baseline.
Root caused per-layer allocation overhead as the primary bottleneck and eliminated it with preallocated global buffers, achieving up to 2 times speedup.
